title: Design useful 404 and error states
description: Differentiate missing content, unauthorised access, validation and temporary failure.
accomplishes: Differentiate missing content, unauthorised access, validation and temporary failure. Specify HTTP behaviour, helpful recovery links and accessible feedback. Preserve useful input and do not disguise a real error as success or redirect every unknown route to the homepage.
prompt:
Act as a web developer.

Task: Design useful 404 and error states.

Input context:
- ROUTES: [ROUTES]
- USER TASKS: [USER TASKS]
- ERROR TYPES: [ERROR TYPES]

Differentiate missing content, unauthorised access, validation and temporary failure. Specify HTTP behaviour, helpful recovery links and accessible feedback. Preserve useful input and do not disguise a real error as success or redirect every unknown route to the homepage.

Preserve the existing architecture, minimise dependencies and define scope, acceptance criteria and relevant tests. Keep secrets server-side. No production changes or deployment without approval.

Use English for explanations unless the task or user explicitly requires another language. Use clear sections and a format suited to the deliverable. If essential information is missing, ask a focused question before concluding. Label assumptions and unknowns. Do not invent facts, sources, results or completed checks. End with verification criteria and remaining limitations.
exampleResult:
## Missing-resource experience
Return an actual 404 and explain that the resource cannot be found. Offer the catalogue and search, without inventing the requested item. A temporary API failure instead offers retry and retains context. Test both status codes and user recovery; a visually friendly error page alone does not establish correct routing.
